name: NIST SP 800-131A Rev. 2
reference: NIST SP 800-131A Rev. 2, Transitioning the Use of Cryptographic Algorithms and Key Lengths: §3 (at least 112 bits of security strength), Table 1 (three-key TDEA disallowed after 2023), Table 8 (SHA-1 signature generation disallowed), Tables 2/4/5 (RSA/DSA/DH >= 2048, ECDSA/EdDSA >= 224).
summary: Baseline transition rules: at least 112-bit security strength, no SHA-1 digital signatures, no three-key Triple DES after 2023.
notes: minimum_security_strength 112: §3 'a security strength of at least 112 bits is required at this time for applying cryptographic protection'. cipher_tags disallow: Table 1 'Three-key TDEA Encryption ... Disallowed after 2023' -> 3des; RC4, single DES and export provide well under 112 bits; NULL/anon/MD5 are not approved. CBC and HMAC-SHA-1 MAC remain acceptable under this standard (SHA-1 is disallowed only for signature GENERATION, and HMAC does not rely on collision resistance), so 'cbc' and 'sha1' tags are NOT disallowed. signature_algorithms.disallow: Table 8 'SHA-1 ... Digital signature generation: Disallowed ...' -> rsa_pkcs1_sha1, ecdsa_sha1; MD5 -> rsa_pkcs1_md5. certificate min_rsa_bits 2048 (Table 2/5 'len(n) >= 2048'), min_ec_bits 224 (Table 2 'ECDSA or EdDSA: len(n) >= 224'), disallow_sha1 (a SHA-1 certificate signature is SHA-1 signature generation). This standard governs algorithms and key lengths, not TLS versions, so protocols are unconstrained.
